narrative:
Scope of capture: 212 storage events (cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage) and 19 window property events, for a total of 231 events considered. Storage is dominated by localStorage (Optimizely, Sentry, analytics) with a single origin (https://www.premierleague.com). Window properties expose a rich runtime config tree and multiple SDKs (PULSE, Sentry, Google IMA, Blaze, OneTrust, Ecal).

TRACE VALUE: The literal value 'TRACE VALUE' does not appear anywhere in network responses, storage (cookies/localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB), or window properties according to search_everywhere; total_matches = 0. There is therefore no origin to attribute for that specific value within this capture.

Auth & tokens: Primary user auth for video/IAS appears to rely on JWTs stored in localStorage under wsc_ias_accessToken and wsc_ias_refreshToken. Both look like standard JWTs (header starting with 'eyJ', three segments) and are written once during the session, with no observed refresh in this capture. A separate wsc_ias_userId key stores a stable opaque identifier for the logged-in user. These three keys together form the core IAS auth bundle.

Session-like identifiers exist in sessionStorage and window properties but are mostly analytics/observability: __spdt and tt_sessionId in sessionStorage for analytics and TikTok pixel; many Sentry session.id/sid values and traceIds in window.__SENTRY__ for error and replay tracking; OneTrustStub.otSdkStub.domainId for consent SDK scoping. None of these appear to be used as primary app auth.

Config & API keys: A large PULSE.envPaths object on window contains environmentIds, OAuth clientIds for a variety of SSO flows (standard login, disable account, update email, under-13 accounts, 2FA pairing/unpairing), as well as firebase.apiKey and firebase.projectId, plus integration-specific keys for Evergent (subscription/payment message identifiers), StarHub (environmentId, clientId, acrValues) and MediaKind (licenseKey, analyticsKey). These are static or environment-scoped identifiers and API keys used by front-end code to talk to various backends. Additional public keys include EcalWidgetV1Params.apiKey / EcalWidgetAPIKey for calendar widgets and the Sentry DSN publicKey contained under window.__SENTRY__.

Data blocks & caching: localStorage contains several sizeable JSON structures for Optimizely (tracker_optimizely, session_state, visitor_profile, pending_events, event_queue, events) and Google Ads (_gcl_ls), plus spdt-* keys that hold batched analytics or session playback events. sessionStorage holds a compact but structured sentryReplaySession object describing the current replay session. On the window object, PULSE.envPaths, BlazeSDK.Delegations, google.ima.* enumerations, and the __SENTRY__ tree together form large in-memory config/state blocks for feature flags, ad handling, widget callbacks, and observability.

Noise: Approximately 81 storage entries were classified as noise (chartbeat, Optimizely bookkeeping keys, TikTok pixel session counters, Adobe/Alloy consent hashes, Sentry flags, general analytics and tracking identifiers). These were counted but not cataloged individually.

Overall pattern: The site uses a hybrid model where critical auth tokens for IAS/video are persisted in localStorage, while a large centralized window.PULSE.envPaths config describes all environment-specific endpoints, clientIds and keys for auth, streaming, and partner integrations. Analytics, experimentation and observability (Optimizely, Google Ads, TikTok, Chartbeat, Sentry) make heavy use of both localStorage and window properties to cache state and identifiers. No CSRF/XSRF cookies or headers are visible in storage/window data, suggesting CSRF protection is either handled via headers/cookies not captured here or is not central for these particular flows. The requested literal TRACE VALUE is not present anywhere in this ecosystem, so no provenance can be established for it from this capture.
